issues.description: The problem UML and description specify an abstract Animal constructor with signature Animal(String, int) (name and age), but the provided solution implements Animal with a single-parameter constructor Animal(String). This mismatch between the specification and the solution is structural and can confuse students about the required constructor signature and how to instantiate Animals.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor signature consistent with the problem statement. Either update the solution and template to provide Animal(String, int) and store the age attribute, or update the problem statement/UML to specify a single-parameter constructor. Preferred fix: modify Animal.java to include a private int age field and a constructor public Animal(String name, int age) along with appropriate getters/setters, and update all usages accordingly.

issues.description: The problem statement and UML declare that Animal has two attributes (name: String and age: int), but the solution's Animal class only declares and manages the name attribute. The missing age attribute is a structural deviation from the specification and may confuse students about required fields and accessors.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the Animal class with the UML by adding a private int age attribute, providing getAge() and setAge(int) methods, and adjusting the constructor to initialize both name and age. Alternatively, if age is not intended to be part of the exercise, update the problem statement/UML to remove the age attribute to avoid confusion.

issues.description: The problem statement's UML defines Animal with two attributes (name and age) and a constructor Animal(String, int), but both the template usage (Main.java) and the solution implementation (Animal.java) use a single-argument constructor Animal(String). This mismatch between the constructor signature described in the problem (and UML) and the actual code can confuse students about whether an age attribute and a two-argument constructor are required.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the UML/problem statement with the code: either remove the 'age' attribute and the two-argument constructor from the UML/problem statement, or update the template and solution to include an 'age' field and a matching Animal(String, int) constructor (and adjust all subclasses accordingly).
